issues.legal_issue: A simultaneous amendment to a provision supplying eligibility criteria operates retrospectively when needed to give effect to the express retrospectivity of a provision that incorporates those criteria.
material_facts: The amendment expressly made the change to the land-status provision retrospective from the commencement of the land reforms legislation.
That provision, as amended, referred to the eligibility categories in the simultaneously amended provision governing when a landholder could lease land.
The respondent relied on the amended eligibility category for a landholder whose spouse was physically infirm and unable to cultivate.
Reading the eligibility amendment prospectively would have neutralized the retrospective operation of the amended land-status provision.
issues.conclusion: The amended eligibility provision was intended to operate retrospectively, so the respondent could rely on its amended criteria.
issues.legal_principle: Retrospective operation is not presumed, but it may be inferred where the legislature's intention is clearly and unequivocally apparent from the language, context, and connected provisions. The court considered the general scope and purpose of the legislation and relied on Main v. Stark, [1890] 15 A.C. 384 at 388. It held that section 157(1)(a), as amended, had to be read retrospectively alongside section 21(h), as amended.

predicates.land_status_dispute: A proceeding concerns the legal status of persons occupying or holding land under a land-reform scheme.
predicates.related_status_provision_made_retrospect: The legislature expressly makes a provision determining land status retrospective.
predicates.linked_eligibility_provision_amended_sim: The legislature simultaneously amends a separate provision that supplies eligibility criteria referred to by the retrospective status provision.
predicates.retrospective_status_rule_depends_on_lin: The retrospective status provision uses categories or criteria defined by the linked eligibility provision.
predicates.prospective_eligibility_rule_would_neutr: Applying only the earlier eligibility criteria prospectively would deprive the retrospective status provision of its intended effect.

issues.definition: When a land-status dispute involves a retrospective status rule that depends on eligibility criteria amended at the same time, and a prospective reading would neutralize that retrospectivity, the amended eligibility criteria apply retrospectively.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation officer's decision on an objection lacks finality when the officer disposes of the issue without following the required procedure of framing it and referring it to the competent court.
material_facts: An objection was made to a preliminary compensation statement concerning the status of land occupants.
The compensation officer dismissed the objection and confirmed the statement without framing an issue and referring it to the competent court.
The officer acted in the compensation role, notwithstanding also holding the office of Assistant Collector.
Proceedings concerning the same status question were already pending under another provision of the land-reform legislation.
issues.conclusion: The compensation officer's order did not finally determine the occupants' status; finality attached only to an order of the competent court acting on a reference from the compensation officer.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 240(F), 240(G), and 240(H) provided for publication of the compensation statement, objections, and referral of an issue by the compensation officer to the court competent to decide a status suit under sections 229-B and 234-A. Schedule II, item 34, identified the Assistant Collector as the competent court and provided for appeals from that court's order. The compensation officer could not obtain the finality of a court order by deciding the issue without making the required reference; the court also noted that the officer should have stayed the matter while identical proceedings were pending.

predicates.compensation_objection_proceeding: A person challenges a preliminary statement made in a statutory compensation process.
predicates.compensation_officer_disposed_of_status_: The compensation officer decides an objection that turns on the legal status of land occupants.
predicates.officer_did_not_frame_and_refer_issue: The compensation officer disposes of the status issue without framing it and referring it to the competent court.
predicates.statutory_finality_attaches_to_court_ord: The statutory process assigns final determination of the referred status issue to a competent court.

issues.definition: When a compensation officer decides a status objection without framing and referring the issue, and the statutory process assigns final determination to a court on reference, the officer's order lacks finality.
